prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1262; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver. Reports a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Vehicle was stopped at the time of impact and the other vehicle was reportedly traveling slowly. Insured states she felt neck and shoulder discomfort at the scene and declined transport by ambulance. Photos requested and assigned to the field appraiser.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney. She confirmed she is experiencing right shoulder pain and limited range of motion since the collision. She has scheduled an evaluation with her primary care provider. Explained the medical authorization form and the process for submitting treatment records. Advised her to keep copies of all bills and receipts.

Entry 3: Field appraisal completed on both vehicles. Front bumper damage on the insured vehicle is consistent with a low-speed impact, and the other vehicle shows minor scuffing to its grille. No airbag deployment reported. Repair estimate received from the shop and under internal review. Liability appears to be disputed by the other driver, so the file has been flagged for further statement gathering.

Entry 4: Obtained a recorded statement from the other driver, who acknowledges the impact but says the claimant pulled forward unexpectedly. Witness contact information noted in the file but no independent witness has yet responded. Requested traffic camera footage from the municipality, which may take additional time to release. Reviewed the police report, which lists both drivers as cited for no violations.

Entry 5: Received the claimant's initial medical records, showing a diagnosis of a shoulder strain with recommended physical therapy. Rental vehicle authorized for the expected repair period. Sent a status letter to the claimant outlining next steps and the timeline for a settlement decision. Diary set to follow up once the treatment plan is complete and the physical therapy provider submits progress notes.
